title: Paths and Folders
intro: The `pathlib` module treats paths as objects. `Path("data") / "sales.csv"` joins parts with the right separator. A path knows its `.name`, `.stem` (name without extension), `.suffix` (extension) and `.parent` folder. Paths can also make folders, list files and read or write text.

questions.prompt: `mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` creates every missing folder and doesn't complain if it exists. `glob("*.csv")` finds matching files.
questions.exampleCode:
from pathlib import Path
p = Path("reports") / "2026" / "march.csv"
print(p, p.name, p.stem, p.suffix, p.parent)
folder = Path("demo_dir")
folder.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
(folder / "a.txt").write_text("hi")
print(sorted(f.name for f in folder.iterdir()))
questions.explanation: `write_text` and `read_text` open and close the file for you.

questions.prompt: Build `path` for `data/sales/q1.csv` with `Path` and `/`. Store its file name in `name` and its extension in `ext`.
questions.solution:
from pathlib import Path
path = Path("data") / "sales" / "q1.csv"
name = path.name
ext = path.suffix

tests.name: path
tests.code:
from pathlib import Path as _P
assert path == _P('data/sales/q1.csv'), 'path should be data/sales/q1.csv.'

tests.name: parts
tests.code: assert (name, ext) == ('q1.csv', '.csv'), 'name should be q1.csv and ext .csv.'

questions.explanation: Using `/` avoids getting separators wrong on Windows or Mac.

questions.hint: `stem` is the name without its extension.

questions.prompt: Create the folder `projects/alpha` (including `projects`), and inside it a file `README.md` containing `# Alpha`.
questions.solution:
from pathlib import Path
folder = Path("projects") / "alpha"
folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
(folder / "README.md").write_text("# Alpha")

tests.name: file
tests.code:
from pathlib import Path as _P
assert _P('projects/alpha/README.md').read_text().strip() == '# Alpha', 'projects/alpha/README.md should contain # Alpha.'

options.text: The text of every CSV file
Paths of the files in `folder` ending in `.csv`

questions.explanation: `glob` yields matching paths; wrap it in `sorted()` or `list()` to see them.

questions.prompt: `path` should be `exports/report.txt`, but comes out as `exportsreport.txt`. Fix it with `pathlib`.
questions.solution:
from pathlib import Path
folder = "exports"
path = Path(folder) / "report.txt"

tests.name: value
tests.code:
from pathlib import Path as _P
assert _P(path) == _P('exports/report.txt'), 'path should be exports/report.txt.'

questions.prompt: The folder `inbox` holds several files. Build `sizes`, a dictionary mapping the **name** of each `.txt` file to its size in characters.
questions.setupCode:
import os as _os, shutil as _sh
for _p in ['inbox']:
    _sh.rmtree(_p, ignore_errors=True) if _os.path.isdir(_p) else (_os.remove(_p) if _os.path.exists(_p) else None)
from pathlib import Path as _P
_P('inbox').mkdir()
_P('inbox/a.txt').write_text('hello')
_P('inbox/notes.txt').write_text('buy oat milk')
_P('inbox/photo.jpg').write_text('jpegdata')

tests.name: value
tests.code: assert sizes == {'a.txt': 5, 'notes.txt': 12}, 'sizes should map each .txt name to its length.'

questions.explanation: Paths carry their own name, so building a report is easy.
`.parent` gives the folder; `.name` is its last part.

questions.prompt: Tidy the `downloads` folder: move every file into a sub-folder named after its extension without the dot — `report.pdf` goes to `downloads/pdf/report.pdf`. Count the files moved in `moved`.
questions.solution:
from pathlib import Path
moved = 0
root = Path("downloads")
for p in list(root.iterdir()):
    if p.is_file():
        target = root / p.suffix.lstrip(".")
        target.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        p.rename(target / p.name)
        moved += 1
questions.setupCode:
import os as _os, shutil as _sh
for _p in ['downloads']:
    _sh.rmtree(_p, ignore_errors=True) if _os.path.isdir(_p) else (_os.remove(_p) if _os.path.exists(_p) else None)
from pathlib import Path as _P
_P('downloads').mkdir()
for _n in ['report.pdf', 'invoice.pdf', 'chart.png', 'data.csv']:
    (_P('downloads') / _n).write_text('x')

tests.name: layout
tests.code:
from pathlib import Path as _P
found = sorted(str(p.relative_to('downloads')) for p in _P('downloads').rglob('*') if p.is_file())
assert found == ['csv/data.csv', 'pdf/invoice.pdf', 'pdf/report.pdf', 'png/chart.png'], 'Each file should be in a folder named after its extension.'
tests.message: Sort files into folders by extension.

questions.hint: `p.suffix.lstrip(".")` gives `pdf`. `rename` moves a file. Take a `list()` of the folder first, since you're changing it.
questions.explanation: Listing first avoids changing a folder while looping over it.
